newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends weaker, hit by U.S. long bond.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends weaker, hit by U.S. long bond.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed weaker against the dollar on Thursday, its first trading day of the year, on fallout from increases in U.S. long bond yields, traders said.
"External factors put the market under pressure," a trader said. "Increases in U.S. long-bond yields took us by surprise."
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 0.4 and 0.1 of a centavo weaker, respectively, at 7.8940/7.8990 and 7.8810/7.8860 per dollar.
Yields on 30-year U.S. Treasury bonds were up to 6.75 percent, from 6.64 percent in late trade on Tuesday, following the release of economic data.
Dealers noted that higher long-bond yields triggered slumps in both U.S. and Mexico stock markets, which exacerbated peso weakness.
Other dealers also put peso weakness down to greater-then-expected primary rate falls at Monday's central bank auction.
"Cetes rates are again not very attractive following last week's falls. It will be important for yields to adjust next week," one dealer said.
Same-day contracts closed earlier 2.5 centavos weaker at 7.8840/7.8890 per dollar.
